findings: The exact repository source is only '算法题：下一个排列'; it does not preserve an API, in-place-mutation requirement, duplicate-value policy, null behavior, or maximum-permutation wraparound contract.
The candidate keeps all of those missing details explicitly labeled as answer-side contracts rather than presenting them as recovered source facts.

The algorithm correctly identifies the rightmost position that can be increased, chooses the smallest available strictly greater successor from the non-increasing suffix, swaps it, and reverses the suffix to obtain its minimum ordering.
The strict comparison choices handle duplicate values correctly: equal values cannot serve as the increasing successor and do not create a false lexicographic advance.
The maximum-permutation case is explicitly defined by the answer-side contract to wrap to the minimum permutation, and both writer and independent validation cover that behavior.

An independent test compiled the actual candidate implementation and compared it with a separately written brute-force lexicographic oracle for all 3,280 arrays of lengths 0 through 7 over {-1,0,1}, plus null, empty, singleton, mixed, duplicate, descending, and integer-extreme boundaries.
The O(n) time and O(1) extra-space claims match two bounded scans plus an in-place suffix reversal with constant auxiliary state.
No project experience is fabricated; engineering/API choices are clearly described as policy extensions beyond the source wording.
